translated_text: Dhritarashtra said: On the sacred field of Kurukshetra, gathered together and eager for battle, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do, O Sanjaya?
original_text:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय।।1.1।।

translated_text: Sanjaya said: Having seen the army of the Pandavas arrayed in battle formation, King Duryodhana approached his teacher Drona and spoke.
original_text:
सञ्जय उवाच
दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा।
आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत्।।1.2।।

translated_text: Behold this mighty army of the sons of Pandu, arrayed by Drupada's intelligent son, your disciple, O teacher.
original_text:
पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम्।
व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता।।1.3।।

translated_text: Here are heroes wielding great bows, equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata, and the great chariot-warrior Drupada.
original_text:
अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि।
युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः।।1.4।।

translated_text: Dhrishtaketu, Cekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best of men.
original_text:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान्।
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः।।1.5।।

translated_text: Yudhamanyu the valiant, Uttamauja of great prowess, Abhimanyu son of Subhadra, and the sons of Draupadi — all great chariot-warriors.
original_text:
युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान्।
सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः।।1.6।।

translated_text: Learn of the distinguished ones among us, O best of the twice-born; I tell you specifically the leaders of my army.
original_text:
अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम।
नायका मम सैन्यस्य सम्ज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते।।1.7।।

translated_text: Yourself, Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa the ever-victorious; Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and Somadatta.
original_text:
भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः।
अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सोमदत्तिस्तथा परः।।1.8।।

translated_text: And many others, all ready to give up their lives for my sake, armed with various weapons, all expert in warfare.
original_text:
अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः।
नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः।।1.9।।

translated_text: Our strength, protected by Bhishma, is unlimited; but their strength, guarded by Bhima, is limited.
original_text:
अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम्।
पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम्।।1.10।।

translated_text: In all strategic positions, each of you stationed according to your division, protect Bhishma above all.
original_text:
अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः।
भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि।।1.11।।

translated_text: Then the grandsire Bhishma, roared aloud and blew his conch, filling Duryodhana with joy.
original_text:
तस्य सञ्जनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धो भीष्मदामोदरी।
हंसैरिव चकारोच्चैः शङ्खान्धध्मौ प्रतापवान्।।1.12।।

translated_text: Then conch shells, drums, trumpets, and horns all blared together with a tremendous sound.
original_text:
ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः।
सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्तु सिहनाद इव द्विजाः।।1.13।।

translated_text: Then Krishna and Arjuna, stationed in a great chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conch shells.
original_text:
ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महती स्यन्दने स्थितौ।
माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रधर्मतुः।।1.14।।

translated_text: Hrishikesha blew his conch, and Dharmaraja Yudhishthira blew his Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew their conchs, Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
original_text:
हृषीकेशो दधानः कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः।
नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ।।1.15।।

translated_text: The great archer King of Kashi, the mighty Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unconquerable Satyaki.
original_text:
काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः।
धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्च पराक्रमी।।1.16।।

translated_text: Drupada, the sons of Draupadi, and Subhadra's son of great prowess, all together sounded their conch shells.
original_text:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते।
सुभद्रापुत्रवच्छैषा घण्टाघोषा विभीषणः।।1.17।।

translated_text: That sound rent the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons, and echoed through heaven and earth.
original_text:
स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत्।
नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलोऽभ्यनुनादयन्।।1.18।।

translated_text: Then, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra standing arrayed, Arjuna, the son of Pandu, took up his bow.
original_text:
अथ व्यवस्थितान्दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः।
प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसम्पाते धनुरादाय पाण्डवः।।1.19।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: O Achyuta, place my chariot between the two armies, so that I may see those assembled here.
original_text:
हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत।।1.20।।

translated_text: Let me see those who stand assembled here, with whom I must engage in this battle.
original_text:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धवान्समवस्थितान्।
कैर्ममा सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन् रणसमुद्यमे।।1.21।।

translated_text: O Vasudhava, let me see the warriors assembled here, eager for battle.
original_text:
योद्धान्पश्यस्व वृष्णिष्ठ यावत्स्थाः पाण्डवाः शत्रून्।
यावदेवास्तु संयत्ताः स्वस्थिताः प्रतिकूलतः।।1.22।।

translated_text: Let me see these warriors assembled here, so that I may ascertain who is fit to fight in this great battle.
original_text:
यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धवान्समवस्थितान्।
मन्येऽहं युद्धविजयं कृष्ण तेषामवैक्लव्यम्।।1.23।।

translated_text: Sanjaya said: Thus addressed by Arjuna, Krishna placed the best of chariots between the two armies.
original_text:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम्।।1.24।।

translated_text: Facing Bhishma, Drona, and all the kings, he said: O Partha, behold all the Kurus assembled here.
original_text:
भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम्।
उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति।।1.25।।

translated_text: There Arjuna saw standing — the fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends.
original_text:
तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितृनथ पितामहान्।
आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातृन्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा।।1.26।।

translated_text: Seeing all these kinsmen on both sides, standing arrayed.
original_text:
श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि।
तान्समीक्ष्य कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान्।।1.27।।

translated_text: Overwhelmed with compassion, Arjuna spoke: Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen standing eager for battle.
original_text:
कृपया परयाऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्।
द्रष्ट्वैमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम्।।1.28।।

translated_text: My limbs fail, my mouth is parched, my body trembles, and my hair stands on end.
original_text:
सीदन्ति मे गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति।
वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते।।1.29।।

translated_text: My bow Gandiva slips from my hand, my skin burns, I am unable to stand, my mind is reeling.
original_text:
गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते।
न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः।।1.30।।

translated_text: I see evil omens, O Keshava, and I can foresee no good from killing my own kinsmen in battle.
original_text:
निमित्तानि पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव।
न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे।।1.31।।

translated_text: I do not desire victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. Of what use is kingdom, or enjoyment, or even life?
original_text:
न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा।।1.32।।

translated_text: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyment, and pleasures — they stand here in battle, having staked their lives and wealth.
original_text:
येषामर्थे काङ्क्खिते नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च।।1.33।।

translated_text: Teachers, fathers, grandfathers, sons, grandfathers, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and kinsmen.
original_text:
आचार्याः पितरस्तथा पुत्रास्तथा पितामहाः।
मातुलाः श्वशुराः पौत्राः स्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा।।1.34।।

translated_text: These I would not slay, though slain myself, O Madhusudana, even for the sovereignty of three worlds.
original_text:
एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन।
अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते।।1.35।।

translated_text: What pleasure shall we have by slaying the sons of Dhritarashtra? Sin alone will overtake us if we kill them.
original_text:
निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन।
पापादेवातृप्तिः स्यात्कृतकर्मणो घ्नताम्।।1.36।।

translated_text: We should not kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our own kinsmen. How can we be happy by killing our own people, O Madhava?
original_text:
तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान्।
स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव।।1.37।।

translated_text: Though these people, overcome by greed, see no evil in destroying their own family and no sin in treachery to friends.
original_text:
यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम्।।1.38।।

translated_text: How then should we not turn away from this evil, when we see the sin that comes from the destruction of our family?
original_text:
कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम्।
कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन।।1.39।।

translated_text: With the destruction of a family, the eternal dharmas are destroyed. When dharma is destroyed, unrighteousness overwhelms the whole family.
original_text:
कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः।
धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत।।1.40।।

translated_text: When unrighteousness prevails, O Krishna, the women of the family become corrupt. When women are corrupted, intermixing of castes follows.
original_text:
अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः।
स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः।।1.41।।

translated_text: This confusion leads to hell for the destroyers of the family. Their ancestors fall, deprived of offerings.
original_text:
सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च।
पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः।।1.42।।

translated_text: By these evil deeds, the eternal dharmas of the castes and families are destroyed.
original_text:
दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः।
उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः।।1.43।।

translated_text: When the eternal dharmas are destroyed and family tradition lost, the entire family becomes contaminated.
original_text:
उत्सादिते कुले मर्यं बध्यते नृप जायते।
पापो बान्धवहन्ता नरकायैव जायते।।1.44।।

translated_text: O Krishna, the slayers of these family members, though committing a grave sin, do not understand what a great wrong it is.
original_text:
दुःखेनाभ्यवहत्या पापे जायते बहुः।
जन्म कर्म च वैविद्यं देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथाश्रमे।।1.45।।

translated_text: If the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons in hand, stand before me, unarmed and unresisting, I would not feel the urge to fight.
original_text:
यदि मे न प्रत्यादेश्यन्ति पार्थ शत्रवः।
यथा स्थिताः प्रतिकूलास्ते करिष्यामि मनोरथम्।।1.46।।

translated_text: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overcome with sorrow.
original_text:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः सङ्ख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्।
विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः।।1.47।।

translated_text: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, the despairing Arjuna, son of Kunti, spoke these words.
original_text:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशो महापथे।
नैत्यं प्रत्युदिरिक्षन्ति विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्।।2.1।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: Whence has come to you this dejection in this critical moment? It is not befitting a noble person; it leads not to heaven and causes disgrace, O Arjuna.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम्।
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन।।2.2।।

translated_text: Yield not to unmanliness, O Partha. It does not befit you. Cast off this faint-heartedness and arise, O scorcher of foes.
original_text:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप।।2.3।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: How shall I fight against Bhishma and Drona, O Madhusudana, who are worthy of worship?
original_text:
अर्जुन उवाच
कथं भीष्ममहं सङ्ख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन।
इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन।।2.4।।

translated_text: Better to live on alms in this world than to kill these great teachers. After killing them, we would only enjoy pleasures stained with blood.
original_text:
गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके।
हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान्।।2.5।।

translated_text: We do not know which would be better — whether we should conquer them or they should conquer us.
original_text:
न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः।
यानेव हत्वा विषिदाः स्मो मर्त्यास्तस्माद्स्थितान्प्रति कौन्त्य किं करिष्यामः।।2.6।।

translated_text: My resolve is paralyzed by the fault of compassion. I ask you: tell me decisively what is good for me. I am your disciple; instruct me who have taken refuge in you.
original_text:
कार्प्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसम्मूढचेताः।
यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्चितं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम्।।2.7।।

translated_text: I do not see anything that can dispel this sorrow which dries up my senses, even if I should achieve unrivaled prosperity on earth or dominion over the gods.
original_text:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम्।
अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धं राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम्।।2.8।।

translated_text: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Arjuna said 'I will not fight' and fell silent.
original_text:
सञ्जय उवाच
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशो महापथे।
शरणं प्रपन्नो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्।।2.9।।

translated_text: To him overcome with dejection, the one who smiles at sorrow, Hrishikesha spoke in the midst of the armies.
original_text:
सञ्जय उवाच
तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत।
सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्।।2.10।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the living or the dead.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे।
गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः।।2.11।।

translated_text: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.
original_text:
न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः।
न चैव नभविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्।।2.12।।

translated_text: As the embodied soul passes through childhood, youth, and old age, so it passes into another body. The wise person is not deluded by this.
original_text:
देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा।
तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति।।2.13।।

translated_text: The contacts of the senses with their objects give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go; they are impermanent. Bear them, O Bharata.
original_text:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत।।2.14।।

translated_text: The wise person whom these do not afflict — who is the same in pleasure and pain, firm and self-controlled — is fit for immortality.
original_text:
यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ।
समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते।।2.15।।

translated_text: The unreal has no existence, and the real is never destroyed. Those who know this truth are not deluded.
original_text:
असत्सत्सद्भयावहं नास्ति तत्र कौन्त्य।
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।।2.16।।

translated_text: These bodies of the embodied self come to an end, but the eternal self is indestructible. Therefore fight, O Bharata.
original_text:
अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः।
अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत।।2.17।।

translated_text: Weapons do not cleave this self, fire does not burn it, water does not wet it, and wind does not dry it.
original_text:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः।।2.18।।

translated_text: This self is uncuttable, inextinguishable, insoluble, and undryable. It is eternal, all-pervading, immovable, and primeval.
original_text:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः।।2.19।।

translated_text: It is unborn, eternal, permanent, and primeval. It is not killed when the body is killed. Therefore, knowing this, you should not grieve.
original_text:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि।।2.20।।

translated_text: Certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead. Therefore, you should not grieve in an unavoidable matter.
original_text:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.21।।

translated_text: As a person puts on new garments, giving up old ones, so the embodied soul accepts new bodies, giving up the old and useless ones.
original_text:
वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।
तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही।।2.22।।

translated_text: Weapons cannot cut this self, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.
original_text:
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः।।2.23।।

translated_text: This self is uncuttable, inextinguishable, insoluble, and undryable. It is eternal, all-pervading, immovable, and primeval.
original_text:
अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च।
नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः।।2.24।।

translated_text: This self is said to be unborn, eternal, permanent, and primeval. Knowing it thus, you should not grieve.
original_text:
अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते।
तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि।।2.25।।

translated_text: Even if you think this self is constantly born and dying, O mighty-armed one, you should not grieve.
original_text:
अथ चैनं नित्यं जातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्।
तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.26।।

translated_text: Certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead. Therefore, do not grieve.
original_text:
जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च।
तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.27।।

translated_text: Some see this self as a marvel, others speak of it as a marvel, and others hear of it as a marvel. Even having heard, no one truly understands it.
original_text:
आद्भूतानि पश्यन्ति देहिनस्तानि केचन।
दैवीस्तानि पश्यन्ति विद्वांस्तस्यैव चेतसा।।2.28।।

translated_text: This self in everyone's body is always indestructible. Therefore, you should not grieve for any being.
original_text:
देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत।
तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.29।।

translated_text: Considering your own dharma, you should not waver. For a warrior, there is no better engagement than a righteous war.
original_text:
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि।
धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाच्छ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते।।2.30।।

translated_text: Happy are the Kshatriyas, O Arjuna, who are called upon to fight in such a righteous war — an open gateway to heaven.
original_text:
यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्।
सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम्।।2.31।।

translated_text: If you do not fight this righteous battle, you will incur sin, abandoning your duty and your honor.
original_text:
यदि त्वेतदनुश्रव्यं प्रतियेत्वा न विज्ञायते।
त्वं स्वाधर्मं निपातं च सुखं च स्वकर्मणि।।2.32।।

translated_text: People will speak of your eternal infamy, and for one held in honor, dishonor is worse than death.
original_text:
अविरता च मां कीर्तिर्गत्येत्यच्युत मानवाः।
येऽभ्यसूयन्ति कल्पेन ब्राह्मण्यं च तदा भवेत्।।2.33।।

translated_text: The great warriors will think you have retreated from battle out of fear, and those who previously esteemed you will hold you in contempt.
original_text:
अभ्यासेन च कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते।
अव्यत्वाच्च भूतानि कर्मण्यस्य विवर्जने।।2.34।।

translated_text: Your enemies, mocking your ability, will speak many harsh words. What could be more painful?
original_text:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून्वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः।
निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्।।2.35।।

translated_text: If you die, you gain heaven; if you win, you enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise, O son of Kunti, resolved to fight!
original_text:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।
तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः।।2.36।।

translated_text: Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, prepare for battle. In this way you will not incur sin.
original_text:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि।।2.37।।

translated_text: Thus I have described to you the knowledge of Sankhya. Now listen to the knowledge of yoga. Endowed with the yoga of discrimination, O Dhananjaya, you will cast off the bondage of action.
original_text:
एषा तेऽभिहिता साङ्ख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु।
बुद्धियुक्तो युनक्स्वास्य योगं कृत्नार्थवित्तमः।।2.38।।

translated_text: In this there is no loss of effort, nor is there contrary effect. Even a little of this dharma protects one from great fear.
original_text:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्।।2.39।।

translated_text: In this path, O joy of the Kurus, there is single-pointed resolve. For those of irresolute mind, this yoga has no fruit.
original_text:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेका कुरुनन्दन।
बहूनां विप्रतिष्ठान्त्या योगोन्यो निष्फलात्कृतः।।2.40।।

translated_text: The Vedas deal with the three gunas. Be free from the three gunas, O Arjuna, free from pairs of opposites, established in the eternal.
original_text:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्।।2.41।।

translated_text: As much use as a well with water everywhere, so much is there in all the Vedas for a Brahmin who knows.
original_text:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेशु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः।।2.42।।

translated_text: Full of desires, aiming at heavenly rewards, they perform ceremonies for gaining wealth and power and rebirth.
original_text:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्।
क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति।।2.43।।

translated_text: For those whose minds are attracted by pleasures and wealth, the resolute determination for self-realization is not formed.
original_text:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्।
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते।।2.44।।

translated_text: The Vedas deal with the three gunas. Be free from the gunas, free from opposites, established in the eternal, without acquisition or preservation.
original_text:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्।।2.45।।

translated_text: As much use as a well with water everywhere, so much is there in all the Vedas for the wise Brahmin.
original_text:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः सम्प्लुतोदके।
तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः।।2.46।।

translated_text: You have a right to action alone, never to its fruits. Let not the fruit of action be your motive, nor let your attachment be to inaction.
original_text:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि।।2.47।।

translated_text: Established in yoga, perform actions abandoning attachment, O Dhananjaya. Being equal in success and failure — this evenness is called yoga.
original_text:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं �योग उच्यते।।2.48।।

translated_text: Far inferior to the yoga of wisdom is action. Take refuge in the wisdom of discrimination. Pitiable are those motivated by fruits.
original_text:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय।
बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः।।2.49।।

translated_text: Endowed with wisdom, one discards both good and evil here. Therefore, devote yourself to yoga. Yoga is skill in action.
original_text:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्।।2.50।।

translated_text: The wise, renouncing the fruits of action, are freed from the bondage of birth and attain the state free from disease.
original_text:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः।
जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ता पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम्।।2.51।।

translated_text: When your intelligence passes out of the confusion of delusion, you will be indifferent to all that you have heard and will hear.
original_text:
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्यच्य पश्यति।।2.52।।

translated_text: When your mind, bewildered by the Vedas, stands firm in samadhi, then you will attain yoga.
original_text:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्नते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि।।2.53।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: What are the marks of one whose wisdom is steady, established in samadhi, O Keshava? How does such a person speak, sit, and walk?
original_text:
अर्जुन उवाच
स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव।
स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्।।2.54।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: When one completely casts off all desires of the mind and is content in the self by the self, then one is said to be of steady wisdom.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
प्रजहाति यदा कामान्सर्वान्पार्थ मनोगतान्।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टस्तिष्ठति परमस्थितः।।2.55।।

translated_text: One whose mind is not shaken by adversity, who does not crave pleasures, who is free from attachment, fear, and anger — such a person is called a sage of steady wisdom.
original_text:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः।
वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते।।2.56।।

translated_text: One who is without attachment everywhere, who does not rejoice upon obtaining good nor grieve upon obtaining evil — such a person's wisdom is firmly established.
original_text:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम्।
नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.57।।

translated_text: When one completely withdraws the senses from their objects, as a tortoise draws its limbs, such a person's wisdom is firmly established.
original_text:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.58।।

translated_text: Sense objects fall away from the one who does not enjoy them, but the taste for them remains. Even this falls away when one sees the Supreme.
original_text:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः।
रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते।।2.59।।

translated_text: The turbulent senses forcibly carry away the mind of even a wise person striving for self-control.
original_text:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः।
इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः।।2.60।।

translated_text: Having restrained them all, sit disciplined, devoted to me. For one whose senses are under control, wisdom is firmly established.
original_text:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.61।।

translated_text: When one thinks of objects, attachment arises. From attachment comes desire; from desire comes anger.
original_text:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।
सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते।।2.62।।

translated_text: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, loss of memory; from loss of memory, destruction of wisdom; from destruction of wisdom, one perishes.
original_text:
क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति।।2.63।।

translated_text: One who moves among sense objects, free from attachment and aversion, with the senses controlled, attains peace.
original_text:
रागद्वेषविमुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन्।
आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति।।2.64।।

translated_text: In that peace, all sorrows are destroyed. For the mind of the peaceful, wisdom is firmly established.
original_text:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते।
प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्यासु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते।।2.65।।

translated_text: There is no wisdom for the unyoked, no meditation for the unyoked, no peace for the one without meditation, no happiness without peace.
original_text:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना।
न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्।।2.66।।

translated_text: For the mind which follows the wandering senses carries away wisdom, as the wind carries away a boat on the waters.
original_text:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते।
तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि।।2.67।।

translated_text: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, one who has restrained the senses from their objects has wisdom firmly established.
original_text:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.68।।

translated_text: What is night for all beings is the time of awakening for the self-controlled; what is the awakening for all beings is night for the introspective sage.
original_text:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः।।2.69।।

translated_text: As the ocean remains unmoved by the rivers that pour into it, so the wise remain unmoved by desires. Such a person attains peace, not the one who craves desires.
original_text:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी।।2.70।।

translated_text: One who has abandoned all desires, moves without craving, without possessiveness or ego — such a person attains peace.
original_text:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति।।2.71।।

translated_text: This is the state of Brahman, O Pritha. Having attained it, one is no longer deluded. Established in it, one attains liberation, even at the moment of death.
original_text:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ निन्द्यान्दुःखसुखं या।
न निर्द्वन्द्वो न च शोचेत्न काङ्क्षेत्सुखं नरः।।2.72।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: If you consider knowledge superior to action, O Janardana, why do you engage me in this terrible action?
original_text:
अर्जुन उवाच
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन।
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव।।3.1।।

translated_text: With seemingly contradictory words, you confuse my understanding. Tell me decisively one thing by which I may attain the highest good.
original_text:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे।
तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम्।।3.2।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: O sinless one, I have previously declared two paths — the yoga of knowledge for the Sankhyas and the yoga of action for the Yogis.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ।
ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्।।3.3।।

translated_text: One does not attain non-action merely by abstaining from action, nor perfection by mere renunciation.
original_text:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते।
न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति।।3.4।।

translated_text: No one can remain even for a moment without performing action. Everyone is driven to action by the gunas born of prakriti.
original_text:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः।।3.5।।

translated_text: One who restrains the organs of action but dwells on sense objects in the mind is called a hypocrite.
original_text:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्।
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते।।3.6।।

translated_text: But one who controls the senses by the mind and engages the organs of action in yoga without attachment — such a one is superior, O Arjuna.
original_text:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन।
कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते।।3.7।।

translated_text: Perform your prescribed duty, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible through inaction.
original_text:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।
शरीरयात्रापि च ते प्रसिद्धिदकरिष्यति।।3.8।।

translated_text: Action performed as sacrifice frees one from bondage. Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform action as a sacrifice, free from attachment.
original_text:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर।।3.9।।

translated_text: Prakriti has produced beings for sacrifice. Let sacrifice be your purpose; who can live without action?
original_text:
सहायं प्रकृतिस्त्वां प्रकृतिस्तान्सहायवान्।
प्रकृतिगुणैर्व्यावाश्रिया निबध्नाति कर्मभिः।।3.10।।

translated_text: By honoring the gods through sacrifice, the gods will honor you. By honoring one another, you will attain the highest good.
original_text:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ।।3.11।।

translated_text: The gods, pleased by sacrifice, will grant you enjoyments. But one who enjoys gifts without offering to them is a thief.
original_text:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः।।3.12।।

translated_text: The righteous who eat the remnants of sacrifice are freed from all sin. Those who cook for their own sake eat only sin.
original_text:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्।।3.13।।

translated_text: From food, beings come into being. From rain comes food. Rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice comes from action.
original_text:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः।।3.14।।

translated_text: Action arises from Brahman, and Brahman from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading Brahman is eternally established in sacrifice.
original_text:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्।।3.15।।

translated_text: One who does not follow this revolving wheel of sacrifice lives in vain, O Arjuna.
original_text:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति।।3.16।।

translated_text: One who rejoices in the self alone, satisfied in the self — for such a person there is no duty.
original_text:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते।।3.17।।

translated_text: Such a person has no purpose in action done, nor any loss from action not done. He has no dependence on any being.
original_text:
नैव तस्य कृतीनार्थो नाकृतीने हि कश्चन।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः।।3.18।।

translated_text: Therefore, without attachment, always perform the action that must be done. By performing action without attachment, one attains the Supreme.
original_text:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः।।3.19।।

translated_text: By action alone, even Janaka and others attained perfection. You should perform action for the welfare of the world.
original_text:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः।
लोकसङ्ग्रहमेवापि सम्पश्चन्कर्तुमर्हसि।।3.20।।

translated_text: Whatever a great person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world follows.
original_text:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते।।3.21।।

translated_text: In all three worlds, there is nothing for me to be achieved. Yet I engage in action.
original_text:
मे यज्ञान्यत्र कर्मणि लोको मम तीव्रतरः।
न हि मे स्वस्थितं किञ्चित्कर्मण्यनुपदिश्यते।।3.22।।

translated_text: If I did not engage in action, all men would follow my path, O Pritha.
original_text:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।3.23।।

translated_text: If I did not perform action, these worlds would be ruined. I would be the cause of confusion and the destroyer of all beings.
original_text:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्व्यां कर्माण्यहम्।
संस्थानान्संस्थितः कर्म प्रजनिष्यामि चानघ।।3.24।।

translated_text: As the ignorant act with attachment, so the wise should act without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world.
original_text:
यथा ह्यविदुर्वाह्वानः कर्माणि कुरुतेऽर्जुन।
विद्वान्यथा कर्मणि तथा कुर्वन्ति विद्विषः।।3.25।।

translated_text: The wise should not create confusion in the minds of the ignorant attached to action. Rather, engage them in all actions with discipline.
original_text:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तो भवार्जुन।।3.26।।

translated_text: Deluded by the gunas of prakriti, all beings become attached to the actions of the gunas.
original_text:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु।
तान्सहिष्णवो मूढाः कर्तुमर्हन्ति भारत।।3.27।।

translated_text: Giving all actions to me, with your mind fixed on the self, without hope, without possessiveness, fight — free from fever.
original_text:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युद्ध्यस्व विगतज्वरः।।3.28।।

translated_text: Those who know this teaching of mine are men of perfect knowledge. Let them act as they wish.
original_text:
ये मे मतमिदं मत्तः परमं वैविदिते।
इमं ते विदितान्नान्यो नेतरो नेतरोऽपि च।।3.29।।

translated_text: One who performs all actions, dedicated to me, established in the divine wisdom, is not tainted by sin.
original_text:
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते।
योगी युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित् पापनाशनः।।3.30।।

translated_text: Know that all sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic qualities arise from me alone, but I am not in them, nor they in me.
original_text:
ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये।
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु वै मयि।।3.31।।

translated_text: This entire world is deluded by these three gunas and does not know me, who am beyond them and imperishable.
original_text:
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत्।
मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम्।।3.32।।

translated_text: My divine powers are very difficult to see. Only those free from delusion see me.
original_text:
अदिव्या हि मम विभूतयो महाभूत्यो गुणव्ययाः।
मां हि त्वा न पश्यन्ति तमोहिताः पश्यन्ति च।।3.33।।

translated_text: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfectly performed, than the dharma of another well performed. Better is death in one's own dharma.
original_text:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः।।3.34।।

translated_text: Better is one's own dharma, though imperfectly performed, than another's dharma well performed. The dharma of another is fraught with peril.
original_text:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः।।3.35।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: What drives a person to commit sin, even against their will, as if driven by force, O descendant of Vrishni?
original_text:
अर्जुन उवाच
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः।।3.36।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the guna of rajas — the great devourer, the great sinner. Know this to be the enemy here.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
काम एव कर्मणो हेतुः कृष्ण नैव कर्मणां क्वचित्।
कामाद्भवति कर्म कर्म भवति कामतः।।3.37।।

translated_text: As fire is covered by smoke, as a mirror by dust, as an embryo by the womb, so is this knowledge covered by that.
original_text:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च।
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनावृतं जगत्।।3.38।।

translated_text: This knowledge is covered by the eternal enemy, desire, which takes the form of fire and is insatiable, O son of Kunti.
original_text:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च।।3.39।।

translated_text: The senses, mind, and intellect are said to be its seat. Through these, it deludes the embodied by veiling wisdom.
original_text:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते।
एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम्।।3.40।।

translated_text: Therefore, O Arjuna, first restrain the senses, then slay this sinful destroyer of knowledge and realization.
original_text:
तस्माद्विश्वं निर्द्वन्द्वं निष्कामं विद्धि सम्भवम्।
हित्वा कामकृतः क्रोधं निर्ममो निरहङ्कृतः।।3.41।।

translated_text: The senses are said to be superior to the body; the mind is superior to the senses; the intellect is superior to the mind; and that which is superior to the intellect is He.
original_text:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना।।3.42।।

translated_text: Thus knowing that which is higher than the intellect, and steadying the self by the self, slay the enemy in the form of desire, O mighty-armed one.
original_text:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना।
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्।।3.43।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: This imperishable yoga I taught to Vivasvan. Vivasvan taught it to Manu; Manu taught it to Ikshvaku.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम्।
विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत्।।4.1।।

translated_text: Thus received in succession, the royal sages knew this yoga. But over a long period, this yoga was lost, O scorcher of foes.
original_text:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः।
स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप।।4.2।।

translated_text: I taught this same ancient yoga to Vivasvan, and now I declare it to you again as my friend and devotee.
original_text:
एवैवाहं पुरा विवस्वते प्रोक्तो भूयो वै तवाहम्।
सम्भवामि स्वधर्मिष्ठः सृज्यमानः स्वशक्त्या।।4.3।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: Your birth is later, yet I remember your earlier births. How can I understand that you are the first born?
original_text:
अर्जुन उवाच
अपरं भवतो जन्म पूर्वं च पश्यामि ते।
त्वमेव सर्वस्य गुरुः कथमेतत्स्मरामि तत्।।4.4।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: Both you and I have had many births, O Arjuna. I remember them all, but you do not, O scorcher of foes.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन।
तानि वै सर्वाणि जानामि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप।।4.5।।

translated_text: Though unborn and imperishable, the Lord of all beings, I manifest through my own maya, presiding over my own prakriti.
original_text:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन्।
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया।।4.6।।

translated_text: Whenever dharma declines and unrighteousness prevails, I manifest myself.
original_text:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्।।4.7।।

translated_text: For the protection of the good, the destruction of the wicked, and the establishment of dharma, I come into being age after age.
original_text:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे।।4.8।।

translated_text: Whoever knows my divine birth and action, having abandoned the body, is not born again; he comes to me, O Arjuna.
original_text:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन।।4.9।।

translated_text: Many, freed from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in me, purified by the fire of knowledge, have attained my being.
original_text:
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः।
बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः।।4.10।।

translated_text: In whatever way people approach me, I reciprocate. Everyone follows my path, O Pritha.
original_text:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।4.11।।

translated_text: Desirous of the fruits of action, people worship the gods. Quickly come the results of action in the human world.
original_text:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्ते देवता विजा।
श्रियो देवता मानुष्ये मनवे धर्मज्ञाः।।4.12।।

translated_text: The four varnas were created by me according to the division of gunas and karma. Though I am the author, know me to be the imperishable non-doer.
original_text:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः।
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम्।।4.13।।

translated_text: Actions do not bind me, nor do I desire the fruits of action. One who knows me thus is not bound by action.
original_text:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते।।4.14।।

translated_text: Knowing this, those of old who sought liberation performed action. Therefore, following the ancients, you should act.
original_text:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः।
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम्।।4.15।।

translated_text: Even the wise are confused about what is action and what is inaction. I shall tell you that which is action.
original_text:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः।
तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्याम्यज्ञानं च यदुच्यते।।4.16।।

translated_text: One must understand what is action, what is wrong action, and what is inaction. The nature of action is profound.
original_text:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः।
अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः।।4.17।।

translated_text: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among humans, a true yogi, and a performer of all actions.
original_text:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः।
स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्।।4.18।।

translated_text: One whose every undertaking is free from desire, whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge — the wise call that person a sage.
original_text:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः।
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः।।4.19।।

translated_text: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, ever content, without dependence, though engaged in action, one does nothing.
original_text:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः।।4.20।।

translated_text: Without desire, free from thought, without ego, such a person, though performing action, performs it as if through renunciation.
original_text:
निराशीर्निष्चिन्तो भूत्वा निर्ग्रन्थो निरहङ्कृतः।
सन्न्यासकल्पितं कर्म स कर्मात्मनि कुर्वते।।4.21।।

translated_text: Content with what comes by chance, free from the pairs of opposites, established in the self, such a person is not bound even when acting.
original_text:
सन्तुष्टस्तत्कतेन चित्तमात्मनि निवेशितः।
आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते।।4.22।।

translated_text: When one sees the whole universe as one in Brahman, then one sees through the wisdom of the Self.
original_text:
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्यच्य पश्यति।।4.23।।

translated_text: Brahman is the offering, Brahman is the oblation, by Brahman is it poured into the fire of Brahman. Brahman is to be attained by absorption in Brahman.
original_text:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना।।4.24।।

translated_text: Some yogis perform sacrifice to the gods. Others sacrifice by Brahman into the fire of Brahman.
original_text:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते।
ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति।।4.25।।

translated_text: Some offer hearing and other senses as sacrifice in the fire of control. Others offer sense objects in the fire of the senses.
original_text:
श्रवणादीनि वैतानि समानेनाथ योगिनः।
स्वकर्मप्रणिधानेन कर्मजं विधिपूर्वकम्।।4.26।।

translated_text: Others offer their wealth, austerity, and yoga as sacrifice. Others practice self-study and knowledge.
original_text:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः।।4.27।।

translated_text: Others control the breath and offer it into the reverse flow. All these are knowers of sacrifice.
original_text:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे।
प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः।।4.28।।

translated_text: Others restrain the intake of food and offer the life-breaths into the life-breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, having their sins burned.
original_text:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति।
सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः।।4.29।।

translated_text: Those who partake of the nectar left over from sacrifice attain the eternal Brahman.
original_text:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम्।
नायं लोकोऽस्य यज्ञस्य कुत्यान्यः स्यात्परन्तप।।4.30।।

translated_text: Many kinds of sacrifice are spread out before Brahman. Know them all to arise from action. Knowing this, you will be freed.
original_text:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे।
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे।।4.31।।

translated_text: The sacrifice of knowledge is superior to the sacrifice of material goods, O scorcher of foes. All action culminates in knowledge.
original_text:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप।
सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते।।4.32।।

translated_text: Learn this by humble submission, by inquiry, and by service. The wise who have seen the truth will instruct you in knowledge.
original_text:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः।।4.33।।

translated_text: Learn the truth by approaching a spiritual master. Inquire with reverence and serve. The self-realized can impart knowledge to you.
original_text:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः।।4.34।।

translated_text: Having known the truth through this knowledge, you will no longer be deluded. Through it you will see all beings in yourself and in me.
original_text:
यद्भूतसङ्गोऽसद्बोधो विद्धि चैनं निशोधयन्।
विज्ञानेन च भूतानि बुद्धियुक्तः सहासि वै।।4.35।।

translated_text: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you shall cross over all evil by the raft of knowledge alone.
original_text:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वभ्यः पापकृत्तमः।
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि।।4.36।।

translated_text: As a blazing fire reduces wood to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all karma to ashes.
original_text:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा।।4.37।।

translated_text: There is nothing in this world as purifying as knowledge. One perfected in yoga finds this in the self in due time.
original_text:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति।।4.38।।

translated_text: The faithful and devoted, with senses controlled, attains knowledge. Having attained knowledge, one quickly reaches supreme peace.
original_text:
श्रद्धावान्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति।।4.39।।

translated_text: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubter perish. There is no world, no heaven, no happiness for the faithless.
original_text:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति।
नायं लोको न स्वर्गो न सुखं श्रद्धारहितस्य।।4.40।।

translated_text: The yogi whose actions are renounced, whose doubts are destroyed by knowledge, and who is established in the self — such a one is not bound by action.
original_text:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्चिन्नसंशयम्।
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय।।4.41।।

translated_text: Therefore, with the sword of knowledge, cut the doubt born of ignorance. Armed with yoga, arise and fight, O Bharata.
original_text:
तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽत्मनः।
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत।।4.42।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: You praise both renunciation of action and the yoga of action, O Krishna. Tell me decisively which is better.
original_text:
अर्जुन उवाच
संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि।
यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्चितम्।।5.1।।

translated_text: Both renunciation and the yoga of action lead to liberation. But of the two, the yoga of action is superior to renunciation.
original_text:
संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ।
तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते।।5.2।।

translated_text: The eternal renouncer is one who neither hates nor desires, free from pairs of opposites, free from ego, delivered from the pains of action.
original_text:
ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति।
निर्द्वन्द्वो निर्महङ्कारो दुःखैर्विगतः कृतान्।।5.3।।

translated_text: The childish, not the wise, speak of renunciation and yoga as different. Established properly in one, one enjoys the fruits of both.
original_text:
साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथक्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः।
एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम्।।5.4।।

translated_text: The state attained by the Sankhyas is also attained by the Yogis. One who sees renunciation and yoga as one sees truly.
original_text:
यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्रोप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते।
एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यि स पश्यति।।5.5।।

translated_text: But renunciation is difficult to attain without yoga. The yogi established in meditation quickly attains Brahman.
original_text:
संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः।
योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति।।5.6।।

translated_text: The yogi with purified soul, self-controlled, master of the senses, identifies with all beings — though acting, is not bound.
original_text:
योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः।
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते।।5.7।।

translated_text: The knower of truth thinks: 'I do nothing at all' — while seeing, hearing, touching, eating, sleeping, breathing.
original_text:
नैव किञ्चित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित्।
पश्यन्शृण्वन्स्पृशन्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन्श्वसन्।।5.8।।

translated_text: Speaking, letting go, seizing, opening and closing the eyes — knowing the senses move among sense objects.
original_text:
प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि।
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन्।।5.9।।

translated_text: One who dedicates all actions to Brahman, abandoning attachment, is not stained by sin, as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.
original_text:
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः।
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा।।5.10।।

translated_text: Yogis perform action with body, mind, intellect, and senses alone, for the purification of the self, having abandoned attachment.
original_text:
कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि।
योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वात्मशुद्धये।।5.11।।

translated_text: Established in yoga, having abandoned the fruits of action, one attains eternal peace. The unyoked, desiring the fruits, is bound.
original_text:
युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम्।
अयुक्तः कामकामी फलाकाङ्क्षी बध्यते।।5.12।।

translated_text: Renouncing all actions with the mind, the self-controlled one rests happily in the city of nine gates, not acting, causing action.
original_text:
सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी।
नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन्।।5.13।।

translated_text: The embodied self does not do anything, nor cause anything to be done, by the gunas of prakriti. The Self is not the doer.
original_text:
न प्रकृतिर्न कर्माणि लोकस्य कुरुते प्रभुः।
न संन्यसनमादत्ते न सिद्धिं समवाप्नुते।।5.14।।

translated_text: The all-pervading Lord does not take on sin or merit. Beings are deluded because their knowledge is covered by ignorance.
original_text:
नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः।
अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः।।5.15।।

translated_text: When ignorance is destroyed by the knowledge of the Self, that knowledge illuminates the Supreme, as the sun illuminates the world.
original_text:
ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः।
तेषां आदित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम्।।5.16।।

translated_text: Those whose wisdom is directed toward that, established in that, whose faith is in that — freed by knowledge, they go beyond return.
original_text:
तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः।
गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः।।5.17।।

translated_text: The sages see with equal vision a learned Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and a dog-eater.
original_text:
विद्वान्भूतभवोद्भवं विश्वं भूतभवोद्भवम्।
वेद च सर्वसम्भवं तस्माद्विश्वहितो भवति।।5.18।।

translated_text: Those whose minds are equal in all beings — having attained the self beyond the gunas — have attained Brahman.
original_text:
इन्द्रियार्थविमूढात्मा विश्वासविमलात्मनः।
सर्वभूतहिते रताः कृत्यं तत्ते विद्धि परम्।।5.19।।

translated_text: With the mind unperturbed, without rejoicing or hating, without fear or anger, established in the Self, freed from duality.
original_text:
न प्रहृष्येत्क्रोध्येत न शोचेत्न काङ्क्षति।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वा चैवाधिकारभूतः।।5.20।।

translated_text: One free from attachment to external contacts finds in the Self the joy of Brahman.
original_text:
बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम्।
स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखं लभते नात्मवान्।।5.21।।

translated_text: The pleasures born of contact are in the beginning like nectar, but in the end like poison. The wise do not delight in them.
original_text:
ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते।
आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः।।5.22।।

translated_text: One who can endure before the dissolution of the body the urges born of desire and anger — such a yogi is happy.
original_text:
शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात्।
कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः।।5.23।।

translated_text: One who finds joy within the Self and is illuminated by the Self — such a person attains Brahman and is liberated.
original_text:
योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरात्मा तु दुर्लाभो बहुशोभितः।
स वै पुमान् वेद यो वेत्ति तत्त्वं निर्ममः।।5.24।।

translated_text: The sages whose sins are destroyed, whose doubts are dispelled, who are devoted to the welfare of all beings, attain Brahman.
original_text:
लभन्ते ब्रह्मसंमिध्धं योगम् आहतं कल्मषम्।
विचिकित्तेन चित्तेन येषां निर्विषयाः स्मृतयः।।5.25।।

translated_text: For those who have control over their minds and senses, who are free from the pairs of opposites, devoted to Brahman — bondage is cut asunder.
original_text:
शान्ताः कामक्योभ्यश्च दुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्।
आत्मनि चैव वर्तन्ते ब्र्ह्मविदो विमुक्ताः।।5.26।।

translated_text: Having shut out external contacts, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, equalizing the prana and apana, the sage who has control over the senses, mind, and intellect is freed.
original_text:
बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम्।
स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखं लभते नात्मवान्।।5.27।।

translated_text: Established in yoga, freed from sin, united with Brahman, the yogi finds supreme happiness.
original_text:
योगी युक्तो भवति कृष्ण योगी प्रभुश्चाप्यमृतः।
सर्वभूतहिते रताः कृत्यं तत्ते विद्धि परम्।।5.28।।

translated_text: Knowing me as the receiver of all sacrifices and austerities, the supreme Lord of all worlds, the friend of all beings — one attains peace.
original_text:
भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम्।
सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति।।5.29।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: One who performs action as a duty, without dependence on its fruits, is both a renouncer and a yogi.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः।
स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः।।6.1।।

translated_text: What they call renunciation, know that to be yoga, O Pandava. Without renouncing desires, one cannot become a yogi.
original_text:
यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव।
न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी सिद्धिं निगच्छति।।6.2।।

translated_text: The yoga of action has been declared for renunciation. One who does not perform action cannot be called a renouncer.
original_text:
कर्मयोगस्तेऽभिहितः संन्यासस्तामसः प्रोक्तः।
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्।।6.3।।

translated_text: When one sees the whole universe as one in Brahman, then one sees through the wisdom of the Self.
original_text:
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्यच्य पश्यति।।6.4।।

translated_text: Let a person lift themselves by their own effort; let them not degrade themselves. The self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
original_text:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः।।6.5।।

translated_text: For the one who has conquered the self by the self, the self is the friend. For the one who has not, the self acts as an enemy.
original_text:
बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः।
अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्।।6.6।।

translated_text: For one who has conquered the mind and is peaceful, the Supreme Self is established. One is the same in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honor and dishonor.
original_text:
जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः।
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः।।6.7।।

translated_text: The sage who is satisfied with knowledge and wisdom, established in the self, with senses controlled — the yogi who sees earth, stone, and gold as the same — is said to be united with yoga.
original_text:
ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः।
युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः।।6.8।।

translated_text: The person of equal vision toward a well-wisher, a friend, a foe, a neutral, a mediator, a hater, a relative, a saint, and a sinner is superior.
original_text:
सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु।
साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते।।6.9।।

translated_text: Let the yogi constantly apply themselves to meditation, being alone, with mind and body controlled, free from desires, and without possessions.
original_text:
योगी सततमात्मानं ययच्छ निरसः शुचिः।
एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः।।6.10।।

translated_text: In a clean place, establish a firm seat, neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, skin, and kusha grass.
original_text:
शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः।
नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम्।।6.11।।

translated_text: Having concentrated the mind there, with senses and mind controlled, the yogi becomes purified through the yoga of self-realization.
original_text:
तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः।
आत्मनि योगी संसिद्धो निर्मलो भवेच्छुचिः।।6.12।।

translated_text: There, fixing the mind on one point, with body, head, and neck held erect and still, one should meditate on the Supreme within.
original_text:
तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः।
देशे न्यस्य चर्मासनं आत्मन्येवावतिष्ठते।।6.13।।

translated_text: Holding the body, head, and neck firm and still, looking steadily at the tip of one's nose, without looking in other directions.
original_text:
समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः।
सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन्।।6.14।।

translated_text: With the mind peaceful, freed from fear, established in the vow of brahmacharya, having controlled the mind and fixed it on me, the yogi becomes one with me.
original_text:
प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः।
मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्तो मे समितो भवेत्।।6.15।।

translated_text: The yogi who is always devoted to this practice, free from grief, and with mind controlled, attains the highest goal.
original_text:
युञ्जन्नेवं सदा योगी विषादो विनोदोऽरिर्मतः।
युक्तो हि विजितात्मात्मा लभते परमां गतिम्।।6.16।।

translated_text: Yoga destroys all sorrow for one who is moderate in food, recreation, and sleep, and disciplined in work.
original_text:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा।।6.17।।

translated_text: When the well-controlled mind is established in the self alone, free from all desires, then one is said to be a yogi.
original_text:
यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते।
निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा।।6.18।।

translated_text: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker, so is the mind of the yogi who is devoted to the meditation of the self.
original_text:
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता।
योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः।।6.19।।

translated_text: When the mind, restrained through the practice of yoga, attains quietude and sees the self in the self, one is content in the self.
original_text:
यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया।
यत्र चैवात्मनात्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति।।6.20।।

translated_text: The supreme happiness, born of the contact with Brahman, is self-established. Established in it, one goes beyond all delusion.
original_text:
सुखं यत्ब्रह्मसम्पर्शमत्सुखं तमनुव्रतम्।
उपैति शान्तिमतिष्ठा योगमेवं समाधिना।।6.21।।

translated_text: Having known that, one goes beyond all sorrow. Established in this samadhi, one is freed from all bondage.
original_text:
स वै पुमान् वेद यो वेत्ति तत्त्वं निर्ममः।
शान्तिमाप्नोति तदा योगमेवं समाधिना।।6.22।।

translated_text: This yoga is the severance from the contact with suffering. One should practice it with determination and with a mind free from despair.
original_text:
तत्संकल्पविबन्धीनं दुःखदोषानुदर्शनम्।
आत्मनि चैव वर्तन्ते ब्र्ह्मविदो विमुक्ताः।।6.23।।

translated_text: Completely abandoning all desires born of mental planning, and restraining the entire group of senses from all sides with the mind.
original_text:
सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः।
मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः।।6.24।।

translated_text: Gradually, step by step, with full conviction, one should become quiet, and through the intellect, hold the mind in the self, and think of nothing.
original_text:
शनैः शनैरुपरमेद्बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया।
आत्मानि मनसि कृत्वा न विचिन्तयेत किञ्चन।।6.25।।

translated_text: From wherever the fickle and unsteady mind wanders, one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self alone.
original_text:
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम्।
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत्।।6.26।।

translated_text: The supreme happiness is born of serenity. One whose mind is serene, ego is subdued, freed from sin, and established in Brahman — such a person attains eternal happiness.
original_text:
प्रशान्तमनसं हेतुः प्रशान्तो ह्यात्मनः सुखे।
समाहितमहंकारं ब्रह्मसम्पत्तिलक्षणम्।।6.27।।

translated_text: Freed from the guna of rajas, through the renunciation of action, the yogi attains knowledge of the self and supreme peace.
original_text:
रजोगुणविमुक्तानां योगिनां कर्मसंन्यासात्।
आत्मज्ञानार्थसंवित्तिं सम्प्राप्नोति शान्तिम्।।6.28।।

translated_text: The yogi, established in the self, sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self, having equal vision everywhere.
original_text:
सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि।
ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः।।6.29।।

translated_text: One who sees me in everything and everything in me — I am never lost to them, and they are never lost to me.
original_text:
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति।
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति।।6.30।।

translated_text: The yogi who worships me established in oneness, abiding in all beings — whatever they do, they dwell in me.
original_text:
सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः।
सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते।।6.31।।

translated_text: The yogi who, through the comparison with the self, sees equal joy and sorrow in all — that yogi is considered supreme.
original_text:
आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन।
सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः।।6.32।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: This yoga which you have described as one of evenness, O Madhusudana, I do not see its steady endurance due to the fickleness of the mind.
original_text:
अर्जुन उवाच
योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन।
एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात्स्थितिं स्थिराम्।।6.33।।

translated_text: The mind is restless, turbulent, obstinate, and very strong, O Krishna, and I think it is as difficult to control as the wind.
original_text:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्।
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्।।6.34।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed one, the mind is difficult to control and restless. But through practice and dispassion, it can be subdued.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम्।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते।।6.35।।

translated_text: For the one with an unrestrained mind, yoga is hard to attain. But for one who has controlled the self, it can be attained through the right means.
original_text:
असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः।
वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः।।6.36।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: Those without faith in this dharma, O scorcher of foes, having failed to reach me, return to the path of death and rebirth.
original_text:
अर्जुन उवाच
अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप।
अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि।।6.37।।

translated_text: O Krishna, have they not been lost — the strivers in yoga — who have had faith but have fallen from the path?
original_text:
कच्चिन्नो भवित्राग्नि भवतो मारुतस्तथा।
इमं लोकं कच्चित्कच्चिन्न पुनर्भविता भवतः।।6.38।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: Neither in this world nor the next is there destruction for him. No one who does good, dear friend, comes to grief.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते।
न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति।।6.39।।

translated_text: Having attained the worlds of the righteous, and dwelling there for countless years, one who falls from yoga is born into a family of the pure and prosperous.
original_text:
प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः।
शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते।।6.40।।

translated_text: Or else, one is born into a family of wise yogis. Such a birth is rarer in this world.
original_text:
अथ वा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम्।
एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम्।।6.41।।

translated_text: There, he recovers the yoga-knowledge of the previous life and strives again for perfection. Thus the fallen yogi is carried along.
original_text:
तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पूर्वदेहिना।
ततो दिव्यं योगाभ्यासो मन्यते कुरुनन्दन।।6.42।।

translated_text: By the previous practice, he is carried along by the inclination even against his will. Even one who merely inquires about the yoga surpasses the ritualists of the Vedas.
original_text:
पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियतेऽह्व्यवसायतः।
जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते।।6.43।।

translated_text: The striving yogi, purified by previous efforts, rises above the results of good and bad deeds and attains perfection.
original_text:
यतन्तो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पूर्वाभ्यासविनाशिना।
संशयं कुरु निश्चित्य व्यवसायात्मिकं कृतम्।।6.44।।

translated_text: The yogi striving diligently, purified of sin, with the mind perfected through many births, attains the supreme goal.
original_text:
प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः।
एकाग्रता लभते परां सुखं दैवम्।।6.45।।

translated_text: The yogi is superior to the ascetics, superior to the wise, and superior to the workers. Therefore, be a yogi, O Arjuna.
original_text:
तपस्विभ्योऽधिको योगी ज्ञानिभ्योऽपि मतोऽधिकः।
कर्मभ्योऽपि अधिको योगी तस्माद्योगी भवार्जुन।।6.46।।

translated_text: Among all yogis, one who worships me with faith, with the inner self established in me — that yogi is considered the best of all.
original_text:
योगिनामपि सर्वेषां मद्गतेनान्तरात्मना।
श्रद्धावान्भजते यो मे स कुतोऽधिकतरः मतः।।6.47।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: Now hear how, with mind attached to me and practicing yoga, you will know me without doubt, in full.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः।
असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु।।7.1।।

translated_text: I shall declare to you in full this knowledge combined with direct realization. Having known this, nothing more here remains to be known.
original_text:
ज्ञानं ते अहं सविज्ञानं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः।
यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यत्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते।।7.2।।

translated_text: Among thousands of men, one perhaps strives for perfection. Among those who strive, perhaps one knows me in truth.
original_text:
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये।
यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः।।7.3।।

translated_text: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and ego — these are the eightfold division of my prakriti.
original_text:
भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च।
अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा।।7.4।।

translated_text: This is my lower prakriti. But know my other, higher prakriti — the living force, O mighty-armed one, by which the universe is sustained.
original_text:
अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम्।
जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत्।।7.5।।

translated_text: Know that all beings have these as their origin. I am the source of the entire creation and its dissolution.
original_text:
एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय।
अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा।।7.6।।

translated_text: There is nothing beyond me, O Dhananjaya. All this is strung on me, like clusters of gems on a thread.
original_text:
मत्तः परतरं किंचित्काश्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय।
मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव।।7.7।।

translated_text: I am the taste in water, O son of Kunti, the light in the sun and moon, the syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in space, and ability in humans.
original_text:
रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः।
प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु।।7.8।।

translated_text: I am the fragrance in the earth, the brilliance in fire, the life in all beings, and the austerity of the ascetics.
original_text:
पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ।
जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु।।7.9।।

translated_text: Know me as the eternal seed of all beings, O Pritha. I am the intelligence of the intelligent, the brilliance of the brilliant.
original_text:
बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम्।
बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम्।।7.10।।

translated_text: I am the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and attachment. Among all beings, I am desire in accord with dharma, O bull among Bharatas.
original_text:
बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम्।
धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ।।7.11।।

translated_text: Know that all sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic qualities are from me alone. But I am not in them, nor they in me.
original_text:
ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये।
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु वै मयि।।7.12।।

translated_text: This entire world is deluded by these three gunas and does not know me, who am beyond them and imperishable.
original_text:
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत्।
मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम्।।7.13।।

translated_text: This divine maya of mine, made up of the gunas, is hard to overcome. But those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond it.
original_text:
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया।
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते।।7.14।।

translated_text: The lowest of men, evil-doers, foolish, and deprived of knowledge by maya, do not take refuge in me. They have adopted the demoniac nature.
original_text:
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः।
माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः।।7.15।।

translated_text: Four kinds of people worship me, O Arjuna: the distressed, the seekers of knowledge, the seekers of wealth, and the wise.
original_text:
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन।
आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ।।7.16।।

translated_text: Of these, the wise, ever devoted and single-pointed in devotion, is the best. For I am most dear to the wise, and the wise are most dear to me.
original_text:
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते।
प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः।।7.17।।

translated_text: All these are indeed noble. But the wise, established in the self, is my very self. He is the highest, devoted to me with single-minded yoga.
original_text:
उदाराः सर्व एवैति ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम्।
आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम्।।7.18।।

translated_text: After many births, the wise person attains me, knowing that Vasudeva is all. Such a great soul is very rare.
original_text:
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते।
वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः।।7.19।।

translated_text: Those whose knowledge is stolen by desire worship other gods, following their own nature, bound by their own gunas.
original_text:
कामैस्तैर्हृतज्ञाना प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः।
तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया।।7.20।।

translated_text: Whatever form a devotee desires to worship with faith, I make that faith steady in that form.
original_text:
यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति।
तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम्।।7.21।।

translated_text: Endowed with that faith, he worships that deity and obtains his desires, which are indeed granted by me alone.
original_text:
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते।
लभते च ततः कामान्मयैवविहितान् हि तान्।।7.22।।

translated_text: The fruit gained by these people of small understanding is temporary. The worshippers of the gods go to the gods, but my devotees come to me.
original_text:
अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम्।
देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि।।7.23।।

translated_text: The unknowing think of me as the unmanifest having become manifest. Not knowing my supreme nature, I am imperishable and unsurpassed.
original_text:
अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः।
परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम्।।7.24।।

translated_text: I am not manifest to all, being veiled by my yoga-maya. This foolish world does not know me as unborn and imperishable.
original_text:
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः।
मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम्।।7.25।।

translated_text: I know all beings, past, present, and future, O Arjuna, but none truly know me.
original_text:
वेदाहं समवीतानी वर्तमानानि चार्जुन।
भूतानि भावितानि च भूतं च मदनुग्रहात्।।7.26।।

translated_text: By the delusion of pairs of opposites arising from desire and aversion, all beings are subject to delusion, O Bharata.
original_text:
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत।
सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं यान्ति पर्थ ममापरे।।7.27।।

translated_text: Those who, by virtue of past good deeds, are free from the delusion of the gunas, take refuge in me.
original_text:
येषामानुभवोऽस्मि भूतेष्यभिज्ञानविभ्रमः।
सदा सर्वाणि भूतानि न मां भूतेषु वै मयि।।7.28।।

translated_text: Those whose sinful deeds are destroyed by their good actions, freed from the delusion of pairs of opposites, worship me with firm resolve.
original_text:
येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम्।
ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः।।7.29।।

translated_text: Those who know me as time, karma, the cosmic being, and the supreme refuge — freed from the pairs of opposites, they worship me.
original_text:
यो मां कालं च कर्म च मद्भावं च परन्तप।
विद्धि वेदैश्च सर्वैरेवं मा न विचालयेत्।।7.30।।

translated_text: Arjuna said: What is Brahman? What is the Self? What is karma, O supreme person? What is said to be adhibhuta? What is called adhidaiva?
original_text:
अर्जुन उवाच
किं तद्ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम।
अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते।।8.1।।

translated_text: Who is Adhiyajna in this body, O imperishable one? And how are you known by the yogis at the time of death?
original_text:
अधियज्ञः कथं कोऽत्र देहे देहिनोऽव्यय।
अवच्छेदो योगमुखेन त्वसौ मे वर्त्म प्रचक्ष्व सुखे।।8.2।।

translated_text: The Blessed Lord said: The imperishable Brahman is the supreme. One's own nature is called the Self. The action causing the coming into being of beings is called karma.
original_text:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावोऽध्यात्ममुच्यते।
भूतभावोद्भवकर्म सम्भवः कर्मसंज्ञितम्।।8.3।।

translated_text: The perishable being is adhibhuta. The universal form of the Self is Adhidaiva. I am Adhiyajna in this body, O best among embodied.
original_text:
अधिभूतं क्षरो भावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतम्।
अधियज्ञोऽहं एवात्र देहे देहिनो वरिष्ठ।।8.4।।

translated_text: Whoever, at the time of death, remembering me alone, leaves the body and goes forth — he attains my being. There is no doubt about this.
original_text:
अन्तकाले च मामेव स्मरन्मुक्त्वा कलेवरम्।
यः प्रयाति स मद्भावं याति नास्त्यत्र संशयः।।8.5।।

translated_text: Whatever state of being one remembers when leaving the body, that state one attains, O son of Kunti, having been always absorbed in that thought.
original_text:
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्।
तमतमेवैव कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः।।8.6।।

translated_text: Therefore, at all times, remember me and fight. With mind and intellect fixed on me, you will certainly come to me.
original_text:
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मां अनुस्मर युध्य च।
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्मामेवैष्यस्यसंशयम्।।8.7।।

translated_text: With the mind not wandering elsewhere, united with the yoga of practice, meditating on the supreme divine person, one attains that imperishable goal.
original_text:
अभ्यासयोगयुक्तेन चेतसा नान्यगामिना।
परमं पुरुषं दिव्यं याति पार्थानुचिन्तयन्।।8.8।।

translated_text: One should meditate on the omniscient, ancient, ruler of all, subtler than the subtle, the support of all, with form inconceivable, self-luminous like the sun, beyond darkness, the wise dharmic Krishna.
original_text:
कविं पुराणमनुशासितारमणोरणीयांसमनुविचिन्तयेत्सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपम्।
आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात्प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुस्थितं कृष्णं प्रणतोऽस्मि।।8.9।।

translated_text: With the life-breaths controlled, moving in the middle channels, the yogi who is devoted, with mind fixed and the goal of liberation in view, meditates on the imperishable Brahman.
original_text:
प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ।
यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः।।8.10।।

translated_text: Those who know the imperishable Brahman, which the Vedic scholars declare, which the desiring ascetics seek through brahmacharya, for whose sake people practice dharma — I shall declare briefly.
original_text:
यदक्षरं वेदविदो वदन्ति विश्वान्तप्राप्तिं कामिनो यदिच्छन्ति।
कौटस्थ्यं यच्चेतसा साधुधर्मेष्वमृतत्वं यच्च कांक्षन्ति भक्ताः।।8.11।।

translated_text: Having closed all the gates, restraining the mind in the heart, fixing the life-breath in the head, the yogi practices the concentration of yoga.
original_text:
सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च।
मूर्ध्यधायात्मनः प्राणमास्थितो योगधारणाम्।।8.12।।
