अकामः सर्वकार्मै फलं त्यक्ता शाश्वतः।
अनासृतः कर्मफलं युद्ध्यस्य कृतनिश्चयः।।18.12।।

translated_text: O mighty-armed one, know from Me these five causes, as declared in the Sankhya system, which are the decisive factors for the accomplishment of all actions.
original_text:
पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे।
साङ्ख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि कर्मभव हेतवः।।18.13।।

translated_text: The body, the doer, the various organs, the many kinds of efforts, and the fifth — the presiding deity — these are the five factors.
original_text:
अधिष्ठानं कर्म च कर्ता हेतवः प्रथमाः त्रिः।
दृष्टं दृष्टान्तमविद्धं च षष्ठं पञ्चमे अविद्धं च।।18.14।।

translated_text: One who is free from egoism, whose intellect is not tainted by the sense of doership — though he slays these people, he slays not, nor is he bound.
original_text:
यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते।
हत्वाऽपि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते।।18.15।।

translated_text: Knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knower — these three motivate action. The instrument, the action, and the doer — these three constitute the basis of action.
original_text:
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना।
करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्तितः।।18.16।।

translated_text: Knowledge, action, and the doer are each of three kinds according to the division of the gunas. Hear their distinctions in brief.
original_text:
ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः।
प्रोच्यते गुणसङ्ख्याने श्रृणु तानि समासतः।।18.17।।

translated_text: Knowledge by which the undivided Brahman is seen in all mutable beings — know that to be sattvic knowledge.
original_text:
ज्ञानं सर्वधर्माणां मोक्षकामैः परिज्ञातम्।
सर्वं कर्माकिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते।।18.18।।

translated_text: Knowledge is declared to be of three kinds, as are actions. Know the distinctions among them from Me.
original_text:
ज्ञानं च त्रिविधं प्रोक्तं कर्मभिस्तस्य ये विदुः।
विभिन्नं चापि तेषां ज्ञानं विभिन्नं च भवति।।18.19।।

translated_text: That knowledge by which one sees the one imperishable reality in all beings, undivided among the divided — that is sattvic knowledge.
original_text:
सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते।
अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं सात्त्विकं परम्।।18.20।।

translated_text: That knowledge by which one sees each entity as separate, with different forms and qualities among all beings — that is rajasic knowledge.
original_text:
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान् पृथग्विधान्।
वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं राजसं स्मृतम्।।18.21।।

translated_text: That knowledge which clings to a single effect as if it were the whole, without reason, lacking in clarity, and confused — that is tamasic knowledge.
original_text:
यत्तु एकस्मिन्नेवान्यत्परं यद्विसृज्यते।
एकत्वमन्यताऽभावं तन्नासं तामसं स्मृतम्।।18.22।।

translated_text: The action that is obligatory, not done for personal desire, performed without attachment or aversion, free from the sense of doership — such an action is sattvic.
original_text:
नियतं सङ्गरहितं रागद्वेषविवर्जितम्।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारं स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः।।18.23।।

translated_text: But action performed with desire, driven by selfish motives, and done with great effort — such action is called rajasic.
original_text:
काम्यान्यभिसन्धाय रजोगुणविवर्जितम्।
कर्म सङ्गिन्प्रवक्ष्याम्यसङ्गिनस्तु राजसम्।।18.24।।

translated_text: Action performed with delusion, without considering consequences, loss, injury, or one's own capacity — such action is called tamasic.
original_text:
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनवेक्ष्य च पौरुषम्।
मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते।।18.25।।

translated_text: The doer who is free from attachment, free from false ego, endowed with enthusiasm and determination, and unbiased by success or failure — such a doer is called sattvic.
original_text:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते।।18.26।।

translated_text: The doer who is passionate, desirous of results, greedy, violent, impure, and subject to joy and sorrow — such a doer is called rajasic.
original_text:
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्षुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः।
हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः।।18.27।।

translated_text: The doer who is undisciplined, crude, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, depressed, and procrastinating — such a doer is called tamasic.
original_text:
अयुक्तः प्राकृतस्तन्द्री निर्विशङ्को विचेतनः।
जूष्यपत्रकृतसङ्कल्पो यस्तत्तामस उच्यते।।18.28।।

translated_text: O mighty-armed one, hear from Me the distinctions of the intellect and fortitude, as also of action, duty, and the impulse for action — all in brief.
original_text:
बुद्धिर्भेदं विधेहि कर्मधर्मौ च तथा।
तथा चाभिप्रयोगं च ज्ञानं प्राहुः समासतः।।18.29।।

translated_text: That which understands the paths of action and renunciation, what ought to be done and what should not be done, what is to be feared and what is not, and the path of bondage and liberation — that intellect is sattvic, O Arjuna.
original_text:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये।
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी।।18.30।।

translated_text: That by which one incorrectly understands dharma and adharma, duty and what is not duty — that intellect is rajasic, O Arjuna.
original_text:
यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च।
अथ यद्भयमुच्यते यथा भयमनुच्यते।।18.31।।

translated_text: That intellect which, covered by darkness, considers adharma to be dharma and all things in reverse — that intellect is tamasic, O Arjuna.
original_text:
अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता।
सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी।।18.32।।

translated_text: That fortitude by which one holds the mind, life forces, and senses steady through the practice of Yoga — that fortitude is sattvic, O Arjuna.
original_text:
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः।
योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी।।18.33।।

translated_text: That fortitude by which, with a selfish desire for results, one holds fast to duty, pleasure, and wealth with attachment — that fortitude is rajasic, O Arjuna.
original_text:
यया तु धर्मकामार्थान्धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन।
प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी।।18.34।।

translated_text: That fortitude by which the foolish person does not abandon sleep, fear, sorrow, depression, and conceit — that fortitude is tamasic, O Arjuna.
original_text:
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च।
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी।।18.35।।

translated_text: O best among the Bharatas, now hear from Me of the three kinds of happiness. That which, through practice, brings relief from sorrow and has a beginning and an end — is called sattvic.
original_text:
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ।
यद्भाव्यच्छोकमुद्विग्नं सुखं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्।।18.36।।

translated_text: That happiness which comes from the contact of the senses with their objects, and which is like poison at first but nectar at the end — that is called rajasic.
original_text:
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यद्भाव्यग्रे विभाव्यते।
सुखं मोहनमारम्भं राजसं स्मृतम्।।18.37।।

translated_text: That happiness which arises from sleep, laziness, and negligence, which deludes one from the path of self-realization — that is called tamasic.
original_text:
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तमसः सुखमुच्यते।
यद्भाव्यनुव्ययश्चापि सुखं तामसं स्मृतम्।।18.38।।

translated_text: There is no being on earth or in heaven among the gods that is free from the three gunas born of nature.
original_text:
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः।
सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः।।18.39।।

translated_text: O Parantapa, the duties of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras are divided according to the gunas born of their own nature.
original_text:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप।
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः।।18.40।।

translated_text: Tranquility, self-control, austerity, purity, patience, uprightness, knowledge, wisdom, and faith — these are the duties of Brahmins born of their own nature.
original_text:
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्राह्मे कर्म स्वभावजम्।।18.41।।

translated_text: Heroism, power, determination, resourcefulness, courage in battle, generosity, and leadership — these are the duties of Kshatriyas born of their own nature.
original_text:
शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम्।
दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम्।।18.42।।

translated_text: Agriculture, cattle rearing, and trade are the duties of Vaishyas born of their own nature. Service-oriented work is the duty of Shudras born of their own nature.
original_text:
कृषिगोरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम्।
परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम्।।18.43।।

translated_text: By devotedly performing one's own duty, a person attains perfection. By being absorbed in one's own work, one achieves perfection without fear.
original_text:
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः।
स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा कुर्वन्न बिभ्यति।।18.44।।

translated_text: By performing one's own duty without negligence and by being devoted to the task, one attains the Supreme.
original_text:
यत्स्वकर्मणा गुणसम्प्रदानस्य साधिकारः।
सम्प्रदायाविरोधेन स्वकर्मणा शिली।।18.45।।

translated_text: By worshiping the Lord of all, who pervades everything, through one's own duty, a person attains perfection.
original_text:
यत्पुरुषेण हिरण्मयेन सर्वं इदं ततं।
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः।।18.46।।

translated_text: Better is one's own duty, though imperfectly performed, than the duty of another well performed. Better is death in the performance of one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with danger.
original_text:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः।।18.47।।

translated_text: Therefore, without abandoning one's own duty, one should never try to perform the duty of another. Even if one performs it imperfectly, the undertaking is not lost.
original_text:
अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः।
तस्मादज्ञानजं ज्ञानं विद्धि ह्यज्ञानसंभवम्।।18.48।।

translated_text: The Lord removes the fruits of one's actions — the result of what was done in the past. By the practice of knowledge, one should seek perfection.
original_text:
हरिः हरत्वविद्यमानं पुरतः कर्मविपाकं यथा।
संसिद्धं कुरु कर्म त्वं ज्ञानाभ्यासेन वा पुनः।।18.49।।

translated_text: O son of Kunti, hear from Me in brief how one who has attained perfection also attains Brahman, which is the highest knowledge.
original_text:
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे।
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा।।18.50।।

translated_text: Endowed with purified intelligence and controlling the mind and senses, one abandons both good and evil deeds. Therefore, devote yourself to Yoga. Yoga is skill in action.
original_text:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।
तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्।।18.51।।

translated_text: When one sees the separate existence of all beings, remaining centered in the One, one moves toward Brahman.
original_text:
यदा भूतपृथग्भावमेकस्थमनुपश्यति।
तत एव च विस्तारं ब्रह्म सम्प्यात्ति देहभृत्।।18.52।।

translated_text: The devoted yogis, freed from the impurities of the mode of ignorance by long practice, attain peace through the Self that abides in all beings.
original_text:
येऽभ्यासयुक्ता योगिनस्तमसो दोषदूषितम्।
सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा शान्तिं लभते जातिम्।।18.53।।

translated_text: Having attained Brahman, the one of peaceful mind neither grieves nor desires. Being equal to all beings, one attains the supreme devotion to Me.
original_text:
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति।
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम्।।18.54।।

translated_text: Through devotion, one comes to know Me — who I am and what My extent is in truth. Having known Me in truth, one immediately enters into Me.
original_text:
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः।
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम्।।18.55।।

translated_text: Always performing all actions, taking refuge in Me, by My grace one attains the eternal, imperishable abode.
original_text:
सर्वकर्मण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः।
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम्।।18.56।।

translated_text: Mentally surrendering all actions to Me, taking refuge in Me, and fixing your intellect on Me, always fix your mind on Me.
original_text:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्न्यस्य मत्परः।
बुद्धियोगं उपाश्रिय मच्चित्तो मत्परो भव।।18.57।।

translated_text: Mentally surrendering all actions to Me, taking refuge in Me, fixing your intellect on Yoga, keep your mind ever on Me.
original_text:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्न्यस्य मत्परः।
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रिय मच्चित्तः सदा भव।।18.58।।

translated_text: If, due to false pride, you will not engage in this fight, you will be compelled to act by your own nature, born of your gunas.
original_text:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्न्यस्य मत्परः।
अथ चेत्त्वं न कर्मणि मां कर्मभ्यो निवर्त्स्यसि।।18.59।।

translated_text: O Arjuna, bound by your own karma, born of your nature, that which you wish not to do, you will do helplessly.
original_text:
कर्मण्यभिरतः पार्थ नियतं कर्म कुर्व हा।
जित्वा स्वं भवाभ्यश्च श्रेयस्ते प्रत्यक्षं कृतम्।।18.60।।

translated_text: The Lord, O Arjuna, dwells in the hearts of all beings, causing them to revolve by His illusory power, as if mounted on a machine.
original_text:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति।
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया।।18.61।।

translated_text: O Bharata, take refuge in Him alone with your whole being. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
original_text:
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत।
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम्।।18.62।।

translated_text: Thus I have declared to you the most secret of all knowledge. Reflect upon it fully, and then do as you wish.
original_text:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया।
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु।।18.63।।

translated_text: Hear again My supreme word, the most secret of all. Because you are My dear friend, I shall tell you what is for your benefit.
original_text:
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः।
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्।।18.64।।

translated_text: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me, bow down to Me. Thus uniting yourself with Me and setting Me as the supreme goal, you shall come to Me.
original_text:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु।
मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः।।18.65।।

translated_text: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in Me alone. I shall liberate you from all sins; do not grieve.
original_text:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः।।18.66।।

translated_text: This supreme secret should never be disclosed to one who is not austere, not devoted, not a hearer, or one who does not have faith.
original_text:
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन।
न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति।।18.67।।

translated_text: Whoever teaches this supreme secret to My devotees, showing great devotion to Me, shall come to Me without doubt.
original_text:
य इदं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति।
भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः।।18.68।।

translated_text: There is no one in the world more dear to Me than he who does this. Neither in this world nor the next shall anyone be more dear to Me.
original_text:
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिद्मे प्रियकृत्तमः।
भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि।।18.69।।

translated_text: And whoever studies this sacred dialogue of ours — I consider him to be worshiping Me with the sacrifice of knowledge. This is My opinion.
original_text:
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः।
ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः।।18.70।।

translated_text: The person who hears this with faith and without envy — even he, freed from sinful reactions, shall attain the auspicious worlds where the righteous dwell.
original_text:
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः।
सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभांल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम्।।18.71।।

translated_text: O Arjuna, was this heard with one-pointed attention? Has your delusion born of ignorance been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?
original_text:
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा।
कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय।।18.72।।

translated_text: My delusion is destroyed. I have regained my memory by Your grace. I stand firm with my doubts dispelled. I shall act according to Your word.
original_text:
नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा प्रतिष्ठिता निश्चिता।
करिष्ये वचनं तव इति मे निश्चितम् मतम्।।18.73।।

translated_text: Wherever there is the Lord of Yoga, Krishna, and wherever there is Arjuna, the archer, there will certainly be prosperity, victory, abundance, and justice. This is my conviction.
original_text:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम।।18.74।।

translated_text: Sanjaya said: Thus I heard this dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, which fills one with wonder and causes one's hair to stand on end.
original_text:
संजय उवाच
प्रमाणे कर्मणोऽस्माकं स्मृत्वैतद् गुणत्रयम्।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं कृष्णप्रीत्या यदाकरोत्।।18.75।।

translated_text: By the grace of Vyasa, I heard this supreme secret, Yoga, directly from the Lord of Yoga, Krishna Himself speaking.
original_text:
स्मृत्वा वसूद्धवस्यैतद् गुणत्रयविभागतः।
योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम्।।18.76।।

translated_text: Sanjaya said: Remembering this divine and wondrous dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
original_text:
संजय उवाच
प्रमाणे कर्मणोऽस्माकं स्मृत्वैतद् गुणत्रयम्।
वासुदेवस्य वचनं तद् भूतं भूतभृत्तदा।।18.77।।

translated_text: Wherever there is the Lord of Yoga, Krishna, and wherever there is Arjuna, the archer, there will certainly be prosperity, victory, abundance, and justice. This is my conviction.
original_text:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम॥।।18.78।।
